title: Silence snapped up for $1.3 billion - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Merck KGaA is acquiring UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash $1.3 billion deal, chiefly to gain divesiran, a liver-targeted siRNA heading into phase 3 for the rare blood cancer polycythemia vera.

insights.claim: Merck KGaA is acquiring UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal valued at $1.3 billion.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Another big-pharma cash takeout of a mid-cap RNAi developer supports M&A premia across the siRNA peer group.
insights.quote: German pharma Merck KGaA is buying UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal worth $1.3 billion.
insights.locator: German pharma Merck KGaA is buying

insights.claim: The key asset in Merck KGaA's acquisition of Silence Therapeutics is divesiran, an siRNA set to enter phase 3 trials for polycythemia vera, a rare blood cancer.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Pharma is paying for late-stage siRNA assets in rare hematology; watch the divesiran phase 3 as the value driver of the deal.
insights.locator: Through the acquisition, Merck gains access to divesiran

insights.claim: Divesiran is a liver-targeted siRNA that silences TMPRSS6, a negative regulator of the iron hormone hepcidin, so raising hepcidin limits iron available to the bone marrow and slows the excess red blood cell production seen in polycythemia vera.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Hepcidin-pathway modulation is a validated-by-acquisition approach to polycythemia vera; competing hepcidin-mimetic programs gain read-through.

insights.claim: Polycythemia vera, in which the bone marrow overproduces red blood cells, raises the risk of cardiovascular and thrombotic events, making red-cell control the therapeutic goal.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Defines the clinical endpoint logic (red-cell control to reduce thrombotic risk) that will frame divesiran's commercial case.
